note: Candidates from the 2026-08-29 dedicated verify pass (data/research/salzburg-verified.json shipped 5 trees) that did not clear the bar this pass. Kept as stock per the standing rule that unverified is a reason not to publish, never a reason to throw away.

leads.name: Jubiläums-Eiche (Kaiser Franz Joseph jubilee oak), Volksgarten
leads.why: Not on the official Naturdenkmal register; known only from a memorial stone and a SalzburgWiki article about that stone (Salzburger Volksgarten, formerly Kaiser-Franz-Josef-Park, Parsch district). Sources conflict on the planting occasion: the memorial stone's own inscription reads '1848-1908' (planted 1908 for the 60th jubilee of Franz Joseph's accession), while a separate blog (Fräulein Flora) states it was planted in 1898 for the 50th jubilee; neither figure has been dropped in favour of the other. No source found confirming the tree still stands today, and no coordinates or exact in-park position found. Needs: a site visit or recent photo to confirm existence, resolution of the 1898-vs-1908 conflict, and a tree-level pin.

leads.name: Eiben an der Ernest-Thun-Straße 7 (Naturdenkmal NDM00249, three yews)
leads.why: Access is genuinely ambiguous under hard rule 10's three tests: the trees stand on private property between a parking area and railway tracks, reachable only 'über die Zufahrt des Hauses Nr. 9' (via house no. 9's own driveway), which reads as a private access way rather than a gate that stands open to the public. A claimed Georg Trakl connection (surfaced by an earlier automated search summary) found no supporting source at all this pass and should NOT be repeated without one. Needs: a source confirming genuine public viewing access, e.g. visible from Ernest-Thun-Straße itself without using the driveway, before this can ship.

leads.name: Fichte bei der Hellbrunner Allee (single spruce, Naturdenkmal)
leads.why: Register entry (protected since 1972, area 754 m², described as a shade-tree cultural relic near the Hellbrunner Allee, Morzg) found in the Wikipedia register transcription but not individually chased this pass for lack of time. Unlike the avenue itself this IS a single collectible point and looked promising; worth checking first in a follow-up pass.

leads.name: Maler-Fischbach-Eichen and Eichen am Ludwig-Zeller-Weg (painter Johann Fischbach's 1851 garden oaks, Aigen)
leads.why: Two separate register entries (three oaks each) both tied to the 1851 garden of painter Johann Fischbach in Aigen, a good shared story. Not individually verified this pass. Aigen is a residential district; needs an access check (public street trees vs. private garden remnants) before shipping.

leads.name: Rosskastanie an der Bachstraße (horse chestnut, Gnigl)
leads.why: Register entry, planted around 1900 in a villa garden per the Wikipedia register transcription, splits at 150cm. Not individually verified this pass; needs an access check since it originates as a private villa-garden tree.

leads.name: Birnbaum beim Hofstetter am Gaisberg (pear tree, Gaisberg)
leads.why: Register entry, over 180 years old per the register transcription itself (a real documented age, not derived), last remnant of an orchard on the Gaisberg. Not individually verified this pass for lack of time; a promising candidate for a follow-up, though the Gaisberg is a c.5km hill outside the tight walkable cluster.

leads.name: Linden in Freisaal (four lindens, planted c.1810)
leads.why: Register entry for an ensemble of four separately registered lindens planted around 1810. Not verified this pass. Needs a judgement call on whether the four read as one compact collectible point (like a folded twin) or should be treated as an ensemble that fails the collectible-point test; check on site or via photo before shipping. 2026-10-08: delivered as szb_018 in data/research/salzburg-verified.json (four lindens around one wayside shrine on a public meadow path, documented planting c.1810, Commons photo).

leads.name: Hellbrunner Allee (the c.1615 avenue itself, ~621 trees over 2.5km)
leads.why: NEVER SHIP AS ONE ENTRY. An avenue of ~621 trees over 2.5km from Hellbrunn Palace's east portal to Schloss Freisaal, the oldest preserved seigneurial avenue in Central Europe (laid out 1615 for Prince-Archbishop Markus Sittikus), with some oaks reputedly dating to the original planting. Fails the collectible-point test exactly as a long avenue does: no single trunk to stand at. See the Fichte bei der Hellbrunner Allee lead above for a single tree from this same avenue that IS collectible.

leads.name: Rotbuche an der Hofhaymerallee 13 (Naturdenkmal NDM00218, European beech)
leads.why: Access is genuinely ambiguous under hard rule 10's three tests. Two independent sources agree it stands on private ground, a remnant of the Gründerzeit Villa Schider garden: the Wikipedia register transcription says 'Sie ist heute nur von Süden her einsehbar' (only viewable from the south today), and the Wikimedia Commons category states outright 'liegt auf einem Privatgrundstück, direkt an der Kreuzung zur Nonntaler Hauptstraße' (lies on a private plot, directly at the intersection with Nonntaler Hauptstraße), roughly 12-15m tall. This may qualify under the 2026-08-13 view-only-tree ruling (visible from public ground, pin marks the viewing place, access states the wall plainly), since Nonntaler Hauptstraße is a public street and the tree is reportedly visible from its direction, but no source confirms the exact viewing spot is public ground rather than, say, across another private garden, and Overpass (which settled exactly this kind of question for Ypres/Leuven) returns HTTP 406 from this environment and could not be used. Needs: a street-level photo or a source stating plainly that the tree is visible from the Hofhaymerallee/Nonntaler Hauptstraße street corner itself, before this ships as a view-only entry.

leads.name: Linde in der Glaserstraße (NDM00078, Aigen)
leads.why: Register: old farmyard linden of the Urbangut in Glas. A rental listing for Glaserstraße 21 places the 'alte Linde' Naturdenkmal in that farmhouse's garden beside the old well, and the 2014 Commons photo shows it between houses behind fences. Somebody's home under hard rule 10.

leads.name: Eiche bei der Glaserstraße in Aigen (NDM00174)
leads.why: Register: mighty oak, relic of an old farm, protected 1980. The only photo (Dumboxp, 2014-06-22, CC BY-SA 3.0 AT) shows the crown over a hedge and fence with the trunk hidden, lifecheck OLD (2014), and no public viewing place or access statement found. Revisit if a viewing point and a recent sighting turn up.

leads.name: Linde beim Pulvermachergütl, Glasenbach, Elsbethen (NDM00136)
leads.blocked_reason: stands in a private garden between houses
leads.why: Register text: summer linden about 250 years old (age derived by the Wikipedia template from a 1976 figure of about 200), two-stemmed crown. Commons photos 2025-03-03 (Flanierer, CC BY-SA 4.0) show it inside a fenced garden among houses. Photo exists but access fails hard rule 10 (somebody's home).

leads.name: Neue Kaiserbuche, Haunsberg, Obertrum (NDM00252)
leads.blocked_reason: dead original; successor is a young fenced sapling, repeatedly vandalised
leads.why: The original 1791 emperor's beech was felled by storm damage in 2004; the registered 'Neue Kaiserbuche' is a 2005 planting, destroyed by vandals in 2008 and replaced again behind a fence. Not an ancient tree. Could appear in a story about the Haunsberg viewpoint, not as an entry.

leads.name: Walser Birnbaum, Walserfeld (Wals-Siezenheim)
leads.why: Legendary pear (Battle of the Walserfeld, municipal coat of arms) but the protected 1887 tree was removed in December 2015 and the current tree on Ederweg was planted that month and is not protected. Wikidata Q865771. Only publishable under a famous-tree reading, as a young replacement, and the page would have to say so; no register entry for the current tree.

leads.name: Linde bei der Plainkirche, Maria Plain (NDM00209)
leads.why: Not remarkable on the evidence: sources say a winter linden planted 1910 (Austria-Forum) or about 100 to 140 years old, girth 1.7 m at designation (SalzburgWiki Plainlinde), 15 m tall. Stands beside the pilgrimage basilica, so findable; ship only if the floor of a reason somebody can see is met.

leads.name: Joseph Joachim Eichen (NDM00258, Aigen)
leads.blocked_reason: remnant of a villa garden, a dwelling
leads.why: Three oaks the violinist Joseph Joachim planted by his music room, protected 2014. The Commons geosearch finds no photo within 150 m and the ground is a villa garden; hard rule 10.

leads.name: Linde in Viehhausen (NDM00127)
leads.why: No photo within 120 m on Commons, no description found, access not established. Register-only candidate with a polygon centroid; no photo or confirmed pin in reach, so not verified.

leads.name: Eichen an der Watzmannstraße (NDM00079) and Eichen an der Faistauergasse (NDM00237)
leads.blocked_reason: plural groups marked publishable=false in the register import (not one collectible point)
leads.why: Register groups of several oaks. Not chased.

unmined_register_candidates_note: Roughly 80 of the 87 register rows within 20km listed in the passcheck brief (data/research/salzburg-register-candidates.json and the fuller candidate set behind it) were not individually chased this pass. This pass worked the tightest ~2.5km cluster plus named parks and sacred sites per the brief, verified 5 trees to a two-source-or-honestly-flagged standard, recorded the most promising unchased candidates as leads above, and stopped inside its time box. The remaining rows carry only a German descriptive name and a coordinate from the register import (no age, no girth, no independent second source attached), so each still needs the same per-tree work done here: cross-reference against the Wikipedia register-list transcription (https://de.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liste_der_Naturdenkm%C3%A4ler_in_Salzburg, which usefully carries designation year and registered area in m² for every entry), then a genuinely independent second source (SalzburgWiki, Wikimedia Commons category, a local blog, or a site visit).
2026-09-06_verify_pass_note: Second verify pass. Confirmed three of the brief's near-published candidates are the SAME trees as szb_001/002/003 (coordinates match to within a few metres): NDM00173 'Pappel am Josef-Mayburger-Kai' = szb_001, NDM00019 'Eiche am Erentrudishof' = szb_002, NDM00091 'Stephan Ludwig Roth Eiche' = szb_003. No new trees from those three register ids; do not re-chase them. Separately verified and delivered 4 new trees to data/research/salzburg-verified.json (szb_006-009): a walkable ~700m Riedenburg cluster of three register trees (NDM00196 Steinbruchstraße oak, NDM00215 Neutorstraße 30a lime, NDM00232 Gärtnerstraße lime, all public streets per OSM), plus one folded twin entry (NDM00075 Platane + NDM00114 Schwarzkiefer im Fordhof, the last two surviving trees of the former Hotel de l'Europe park, now inside the Fordhof housing estate courtyard near the Hauptbahnhof). These 5 register ids can be crossed off the unmined pile. NDM00243 'Rosskastanie an der Bachstraße' was already a lead above (unchanged this pass). Stories written and merged same day: szb_006-009 are live in data/cities/salzburg.json, Salzburg now at 9 trees.
2026-09-25_verify_pass_note: Third verify pass, worked a new ~2km Aigen/Morzg cluster south of the existing walk. Delivered 3 new trees to data/research/salzburg-verified.json (szb_010-012): NDM00202 Hainbuche am Freisaalweg (Nonntal, beside the public Akademiestraße car park), NDM00251 Eiche an der Aigner Straße 9 (Aigen, courtyard oak the register itself calls unrestricted), NDM00206 Eiche an der Buchholzhofstraße (Morzg, on the public Buchholzhofstraße path toward Hellbrunner Allee). All three cross-checked against a genuinely independent second source beyond the register/Wikipedia transcription: a dated, geotagged Wikimedia Commons photograph from a different contributor in each case (2014), which also confirmed the tree-level coordinate closely enough to mark location_precision confirmed. None of these three carry a documented age or girth; all flagged for that reason per the standing rule that a missing age never holds a tree back. NDM00218 Rotbuche an der Hofhaymerallee moved to a new lead above rather than shipped: two sources agree it stands on private ground (a remnant of the Villa Schider garden) and the 'only visible from the south' detail was not strong enough to confirm as a public viewing spot without an OSM access check, which Overpass could not answer from this environment (see hosts-that-hung note in the pass report). These four register ids (NDM00202, NDM00206, NDM00218, NDM00251) can be crossed off the unmined pile.
2026-10-08_verify_pass_note: Fourth verify pass. Delivered szb_016 Tofferl Oak, szb_017 Sycamore of Schartenbauer, szb_018 Lindens of Freisaal. Rejects above. Technique that worked: a Commons geosearch at each register centroid (radius 120 m) shows within seconds which candidates have an openly licensed photo at the spot; the viewing of one 500px thumbnail then settles access (hiking signpost at the maple, a private garden at the Pulvermachergut linden). Wikipedia list raw text for Salzburg-Umgebung and Hallein districts gives girth, height and designation date per register id. Commons API rate-limits after about 10 quick calls (429).
2026-10-08_fifth_verify_pass_note: Fifth pass. Delivered szb_019 Dorflinde in Faistenau (NDM00020) and szb_020 Gschirrnlinde in Eugendorf (NDM00199). The four READY leads were re-read and stay leads: Eiche bei der Glaserstrasse NDM00174 (only photo shows crown over hedge, lifecheck OLD 2014, no viewing place or access statement); Walser Birnbaum (protected 1887 tree removed Dec 2015, current tree planted that month, not protected); Linde bei der Plainkirche NDM00209 (planted c.1910, girth 1.7 m, nothing sets it apart); Linde in Viehhausen NDM00127 (no photo, no description, no access, no confirmed pin). Not chased: Linde beim Feuerwehrhaus Elsbethen NDM00210 (Commons geosearch 150 m empty, no photo or exact pin in reach); Eichengruppe am Wolfsgartenweg NDM00070 and Baumgruppe am Fuchshuegel NDM00080 (register publishable=false, so never ship).
